scope: What 1.0.0.11's first session on real hardware showed, put right: the automatic bitrate gets a fresh start when the headset PC's GPU clock is raised, and a second in which frames never arrived (the rendering PC sent nothing) no longer counts against it; the headset PC holds the GPU clock the last session needed from the start (Bazzite); the rendering PC's add-on warning lists only add-ons registered from outside SteamVR. Also the tidier top level of the repository. Every package carries version 1.0.0.12; the native programs are 1.0.0.11's with the new version label and the host's driver is 1.0.0.9's.

from_the_session.what: 1.0.0.11 at Native (2560 x 2560 per eye, 75 Hz) with eye-tracked foveation on a handheld headset PC on Bazzite, wired, Beat Saber, about nine minutes; from the two reports the maintainer sent.
went_well: the sharp region following the eyes for 98.5 % of frames
five frames lost in nine minutes
about 40 ms from the rendering PC's frame to the headset
put_right: the bitrate stepped 65 -> 50 -> 40 -> 30 Mbit/s in the first 80 s, while the GPU sat at 800 MHz and the game started; after the companion held 1300 MHz at four and a half minutes the stream ran clean, but three steps down asked for 160 clean seconds before a step up and the rendering PC's stalls (40-80 ms without a frame, about every half minute) broke every run, so it stayed at 30
the GPU clock was found afresh four and a half minutes in
the host page listed SteamVR's own drivers (indexcontroller, frame_hmd, frame_controller, prism, roy, tundra_labs) as third-party add-ons and suggested turning them off
from_the_session.not_put_right: the rendering PC's stalls themselves: its capture timed out waiting for SteamVR's frame about every half minute (SteamVR logged the handoff timing out 33 times in nine minutes of Beat Saber, and not at all in a longer session with no game); the capture waits up to 10 ms per frame, as ALVR's does. Also the menu button: each of five presses showed unread=1 with no system event.

changes: launcher/stream_budget.py: frames_missing (the refresh rate less the frames received); a second with at least 1.5 frames missing and nothing lost on the network is a source gap, neither late nor uneven, and its arrival gap stays out of the arrival check; fresh_start(reason): back to the session's starting bitrate when it is lower, any pending check dropped, 8 s not judged, the next step up after 40 clean seconds again; the wait before a step up doubles with each step down since the start or the last fresh start (40 s to at most 160 s); the snapshot counts fresh_starts
launcher/app.py: when the session tuning raises the GPU clock, the bitrate governor gets a fresh start and the page's note says so (back to the start: the GPU clock was raised)

launcher/session_tuning.py: the clock a session ended up holding remembered in gpu-clock.json in the state folder, with the GPU's maximum clock and whether it was on the charger; held as soon as the next session's video is up when the GPU's level is automatic and the GPU and power source match; forgotten when a session sets it back down or it is changed elsewhere; frames that never arrived are not counted as running late

host/addons.py: only drivers registered with SteamVR from outside its own folders (openvrpaths' external_drivers), leaving out VROSTBridge's own, any inside SteamVR's own folders, duplicates and those switched off in steamvr.vrsettings; Bigscreen's helpers recognised by their folder as well as their name; the name list of SteamVR's drivers is gone

tests: tests/test_vrostbridge_1012.py (19 of its own, the 1.0.0.11 session's numbers among them); the add-on expectation in tests/test_rc3_updates.py; tests/test_vrostbridge_1011.py's version test accepts later releases

A tidier top level (made after 1.0.0.11 was released): the build and start scripts and the desktop shortcuts in scripts/, the Windows client's CMake toolchain in scripts/cross/, the client's runtime assets in client/assets/, CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md in .github/, the start page in docs/
Version 1.0.0.12 on every package; the release notes, the GitHub release text, the documents and both PDFs; 1.0.0.11's release notes moved to docs/history/
